- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.0–0.3) and price is trending upward, model frequently underestimates upside; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture momentum.  
- When sentiment is positive (last 3 days > 0.3) and price is near recent high, model often overestimates continuation; cap forecast at 1–2% below prior peak to avoid overbought bias.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.3–0.8% to first 5 days to account for lagged sentiment impact.
